paper_summary: Epoxy (bis-A / cycloaliphatic amine) syntactic foams filled with K15 glass-clad hollow silica microballoons (40 um mean diameter, 0.15 g/cm3 bulk density) at 10-50 vol% were cast under vacuum in a planetary centrifugal mixer and characterised for density, total/effective porosity (density-based and SEM area analysis) and three-point flexural performance per ASTM D790. Density fell nearly linearly from 1.15 g/cm3 (neat epoxy) to 0.63 g/cm3 at 50 vol%, while total porosity rose from 2.7% to 18.4% and effective (interconnected) porosity from 0.9% to 13.6%, with a sharp percolation jump above 30 vol%. Flexural strength and modulus peaked at 30 vol% (96 MPa, 3.12 GPa) and then dropped sharply at 40-50 vol% because of microballoon agglomeration, shell collapse and interstitial voids.

processing.matrix_name: bis-A epoxy resin cured with cycloaliphatic amine hardener (100:30 phr)

structure.microstructure_notes: Total porosity P_t = 2.7% (density-based); effective (interconnected) porosity P_e = 0.9% from SEM area-fraction analysis.

test.specimen_notes: 150 x 20 x 3 mm cast coupons, three-point bending, span/depth = 16, cross-head rate 1 mm/min; conditioned 48 h at 23 +/- 2 C and 50 +/- 5 % RH.

evidence.quote: Without microballoon's the initial density of 1.15 g cm⁻³ drops to just 0.63 g cm⁻³ at φ = 50 %, resulting in an overall mass density reduction of about 45 %.
evidence.location: Sec. Results, Density vs volume fraction (Figure 1 discussion)

evidence.quote: In the range of 0–30 vol%, the addition of filler successfully increased the flexural strength (σ_f) from 85 ± 3 MPa to 96 ± 3 MPa and the flexural modulus (E_f) from 2.69 ± 0.07 GPa to 3.12 ± 0.05 GPa.
P_t, which reflects all voids, both closed and open rises almost linearly, from 2.7 % to 18.4 % ... In contrast, P_e, the truly interconnected pores, starts much lower (0.9 %)
evidence.location: Sec. Results, Total and Effective Porosity (Figure 2 discussion)

processing.matrix_name: bis-A epoxy resin cured with cycloaliphatic amine hardener (100:30 phr)

structure.microstructure_notes: Effective (interconnected) porosity P_e = 4.3% at 30 vol%; uniform microsphere dispersion, closed cells dominate. Measured density not stated numerically (paper only states a 28% density reduction at this loading).

test.specimen_notes: 150 x 20 x 3 mm cast coupons, three-point bending, span/depth = 16, cross-head rate 1 mm/min; conditioned 48 h at 23 +/- 2 C and 50 +/- 5 % RH.

evidence.quote: In the range of 0–30 vol%, the addition of filler successfully increased the flexural strength (σ_f) from 85 ± 3 MPa to 96 ± 3 MPa and the flexural modulus (E_f) from 2.69 ± 0.07 GPa to 3.12 ± 0.05 GPa.
P_e, the truly interconnected pores, starts much lower (0.9 %) and increases only gradually up to φ ≈ 30 % (4.3 %).
evidence.location: Sec. Results, Total and Effective Porosity (Figure 2 discussion)

evidence.quote: The optimal microsphere loading was found at 30 vol% K15, achieving a 28 % reduction in density without a significant rise in porosity.

processing.matrix_name: bis-A epoxy resin cured with cycloaliphatic amine hardener (100:30 phr)

structure.microstructure_notes: Effective porosity P_e = 9.7% at 40 vol%; agglomeration, poorly wetted clusters and collapsed microspheres appear, marking the onset of pore percolation (open-cell transition at 35-40 vol%).

test.specimen_notes: Density/porosity characterisation only (displacement method plus SEM area-fraction analysis); flexural values at this loading are shown only in Figure 3 and are not stated numerically.

evidence.quote: Beyond this threshold, P_e jumps sharply (9.7 % at 40 % and 13.6 % at 50 %), indicating pore percolation: an open-pore network has formed, so more voids become interconnected.
evidence.location: Sec. Results, Total and Effective Porosity (Figure 2 discussion)

evidence.quote: Morphological analysis revealed uniform microsphere dispersion up to 30 vol%, while agglomeration and inter-binder voids emerged beyond 40 vol%, leading to uncontrolled porosity growth.

processing.matrix_name: bis-A epoxy resin cured with cycloaliphatic amine hardener (100:30 phr)

structure.microstructure_notes: Total porosity P_t = 18.4%, effective (interconnected) porosity P_e = 13.6%; open-pore network, poorly wetted clusters and collapsed microspheres. Density departs from rule-of-mixtures line above 40 vol% due to trapped air.

test.specimen_notes: 150 x 20 x 3 mm cast coupons, three-point bending, span/depth = 16, cross-head rate 1 mm/min. Absolute flexural strength/modulus at 50 vol% are not stated (only a 35% strength and 33% modulus drop relative to the 30 vol% peak).

evidence.quote: The experimental results demonstrated a near-linear reduction in density from 1.15 g cm⁻³ (0 vol%) to 0.63 g cm⁻³ (50 vol%), whereas porosity exhibited an exponential increase from 2.7 % to 18.4 %.
Beyond this threshold, P_e jumps sharply (9.7 % at 40 % and 13.6 % at 50 %), indicating pore percolation
evidence.location: Sec. Results, Total and Effective Porosity (Figure 2 discussion)

evidence.quote: However, above 30 vol%, a saturation point is reached: particle aggregation, increased porosity, and weakened interfacial bonding trigger a drastic decline at φ = 50%, σ_f drops by 35%, and E_f decreases by 33% compared to the peak value.

extraction_notes: Short journal paper with no data tables; all numeric values come from text/abstract statements about Figures 1-3. Records were created only for the loadings whose values are stated numerically (0, 30, 40, 50 vol%). The 10 and 20 vol% specimens were fabricated and appear in Figures 1-3, but no numeric density, porosity or flexural values are given for them, so they were omitted rather than read off the plots. Unit conversions: flexural modulus GPa -> MPa (2.69 GPa = 2690 MPa; 3.12 GPa = 3120 MPa); porosity percentages -> fractions (2.7% = 0.027, 18.4% = 0.184). Total porosity P_t (density-based, (rho_th - rho_exp)/rho_th) was mapped to structure.matrix_porosity_fraction and the SEM-derived effective porosity P_e recorded in microstructure_notes; note that in this paper P_t also includes the intended hollow-microballoon void volume, so it is not purely unintended matrix porosity. Values that are derivable but not stated were left null and are noted here: the 30 vol% density (abstract states a 28% reduction from 1.15 g/cm3, i.e. ~0.83 g/cm3) and the 50 vol% flexural strength/modulus (stated 35% and 33% drops from the 96 MPa / 3.12 GPa peak, i.e. ~62 MPa and ~2.09 GPa). Particle 'bulk density 0.15 g/cm3' was reported for K15 but is a bulk (tapped) density, not a true particle density, so particle_true_density_g_cc was left null. Test temperature taken as the 23 +/- 2 C conditioning/lab temperature; cross-head rate 1 mm/min was not converted to a strain rate. Cure was 24 h at room temperature plus 2 h post-cure at 60 C; 60 C recorded as the process temperature.
